services/hub/internal/supervisor/supervi.review: Plugin sidecars retain owned start/stop, restart after failed launch or exit, capped exponential backoff with uptime reset, live PID/status/error events, health transitions without restart-on-unhealthy, parent EOF/PID signals, and opt-in separate stdout/stderr streams. Source and deterministic/actual-process tests cover cap/reset/overflow, two-second HTTP budget, crash restart, health failure, quiet default, shutdown ordering/reaping and graceful flush. Go brain/MCP child supervision is replaced by owned Backend services, not hidden replacement binaries. Rust serial health probes are completion-relative rather than a Go fixed ticker; initial Starting is internal only. Environment inheritance now deliberately scrubs owner credentials before explicit child overlays. NativeChild owns/reaps the direct Unix child; do not infer general Unix descendant-group confinement from this mapping.

Mapped start/stop/restart, backoff doubling/cap/overflow and uptime reset, healthy/unhealthy transitions, log stdout/stderr/partial tail and quiet default to named Rust fake-process and real-process fixtures. Runtime shutdown proves broker remains available for plugin revocation before direct-child reap. The actual worker-loop cap test and 1.1-second response fixture pin scheduling/HTTP timeout semantics. Added self-executable two-MiB SIGTERM flush regression that failed under the previous wait-without-drain loop and passes after bounded drains. Linux plugin_manager21 and supervisor_shutdown1 passed; Windows process ownership has separate actual CI coverage and remains a platform gate at final head.

services/hub/internal/supervisor/logwrit.review: Preserves opt-in stream identity, newline records and final partial output without adding unowned copier threads. Nonblocking bounded pipe drains continue during graceful termination so cooperative flush cannot deadlock. Explicit intentional framing differences: Rust caps unterminated chunks at64KiB, decodes malformed UTF-8 lossily, and trims CR; Go buffered unlimited lines and removed only LF. This is not byte-identical log transport and neither implementation promises to scrub secrets printed by plugin code.

services/hub/internal/supervisor/inherit.review: The InheritOutput mode was used for the Go brain child. That subprocess and inherited-pipe mode are retired: owned Rust Backend startup failures propagate through the library/CLI, while third-party plugin output remains quiet by default or explicitly streamed. The quiet native sidecar test pins absence of captured log pipes; standalone CLI/Backend ownership tests pin startup and shutdown without a private companion. This mapping does not claim a byte-for-byte inherited brain stream.

services/hub/internal/supervisor/termina.review: Retains direct-child SIGTERM, five-second grace, forced kill fallback, then reap. During grace Rust now drains bounded stdout/stderr pipes, preserving cooperative TERM output; the real self-executable fixture proved the previous five-second forced-kill failure and now completes gracefully. Runtime plugin shutdown and process-stream fixtures cover reap and final tail. Go also targeted the direct process; this row does not certify arbitrary Unix descendant cleanup.

Retains direct-child force termination on Windows and strengthens descendant ownership with a kill-on-close job. Shared child_job launches suspended, assigns the job before user code, then resumes; plugin adapter uses this exact helper. Exact-source Windows probe and actual Windows04322791 ownership suite (26 tests) passed, including immediate-fork races; final-head Windows CI remains required. Unix graceful flush test is intentionally not evidence for Windows execution.
